subject: lighthouse
pitch: A cozy lighthouse diorama on a tiny rocky island. A red-and-white striped tower with a glowing lantern room and a black iron balcony, a keeper's cottage with a crooked chimney and a blue door, a wooden jetty with a rowboat tied to it, a couple of seagulls, tufts of grass and wildflowers between the rocks, and turquoise water with white foam around the shore, all on a round display base.
reasoning:
Since I only have partial knowledge of the SDK reference, I should play it safe by using createBuilder with a basic root joint called "base" at the origin, then attaching parts to it, trusting the general builder/joint/part pattern even though I'm unsure of the exact part signature.

Given the uncertainty around the exact part() API, I decide it's safer to build with plain THREE.js meshes added directly to b.root, sidestepping the unknown geometry/color argument order entirely while still using createBuilder and rng. I'm now sketching the diorama's layout in meters: a dark wood base disk, a turquoise water layer, a rocky island with grass on top, and a striped tower, planning out radii and heights for each component.

Continuing that design, I'm detailing the tower's candy-stripe frustum sections, a railed gallery, a glowing lantern with a conical roof and light-beam cones, plus a small cottage with an extruded triangular roof, crooked chimney, and colored door/windows, and finally a wooden jetty with a rowboat moored at the end.

I'm sketching the rowboat as a scaled hemisphere hull with a darker inner shell and a rope line, then adding seagulls made from spheres, cones, and boxes perched on the jetty post and roof ridge, scattered grass tufts and flowers around the island, and foam rings near the shoreline for texture.

Now I'm scattering gray flat-shaded rocks around the island's edge, building a shared material cache, and writing a helper function to place geometry with position and rotation options. I'm also constructing the roof as an extruded triangular gable shape, rotating it so the ridge runs the right direction relative to the cottage door.

Then I work out positions: cottage near one side with its tower, the island's grass radius versus overall base radius, a jetty extending from the island edge out over the water with posts and a deck, and a small boat floating nearby on the water surface.
